areas.name: Platform core
areas.description: The nouns every other area is scoped by: who is acting, which project, which environment, which version.

areas.name: Delivery
areas.description: What was built and where it runs — source, pipelines, containers, published contracts.

areas.name: Quality
areas.description: What was tested, when, and how it performed.

entities.name: project
entities.description: A unit of work everything else is reported against.
impact: Deleting a project orphans every version, item and execution scoped to it.

properties.name: code
properties.meaning: short unique handle used in URLs and imports

entities.name: environment
entities.description: A named deployment target a version can be observed in.
impact: Metrics and executions are only comparable within one environment.

entities.name: version
entities.description: A released state of a project that results can be attributed to.
impact: Attributing a result to the wrong version makes a trend meaningless.

entities.name: user
entities.description: The person or service account a recorded action is attributed to.
impact: An action with no user cannot be audited.

entities.name: repository
entities.description: A source repository whose commits are tracked against a project.
impact: Removing a repository breaks the commit-to-version attribution chain.

entities.name: commit
entities.description: One recorded change in a repository.
impact: A commit is immutable; correcting one means recording another.

entities.name: pipeline
entities.description: A defined sequence of automated steps that builds or verifies a project.
impact: Changing a pipeline definition changes what every later execution means.

entities.name: pipeline execution
entities.description: One run of a pipeline, with its status and timings.
impact: A run's status is the evidence a version was buildable at a point in time.

entities.name: pod
entities.description: A running container group observed in a Kubernetes cluster.
impact: Pod state is observed, never authored: it reflects the cluster, so it can disagree with what was deployed.

entities.name: api spec
entities.description: A published contract document a service declares itself by.
impact: A spec that drifts from the running service invalidates every claim derived from it.

properties.name: freshness
properties.meaning: how recently the document was re-read from the service

entities.name: test item
entities.description: One thing to be verified, at whatever granularity the team records it.
impact: Changing an item's meaning silently changes what every past execution of it proved.

properties.name: priority
properties.meaning: how urgently a failure must be acted on

properties.name: status
properties.meaning: where the item is in its own lifecycle

entities.name: test cycle
entities.description: A bounded set of test items run together against one version.
impact: Reopening a closed cycle changes a result somebody has already reported on.

entities.name: test execution
entities.description: One attempt at one test item, with its outcome.
impact: An execution is the only evidence an item ever passed.

entities.name: metric
entities.description: A recorded performance measurement attributable to a version and environment.
impact: A metric without both a version and an environment cannot be compared to any other.
